task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: Global temperature extremes reveal two distinct patterns. By average temperature, the Middle East dominates: Ar Riyadh (45.0°C) ranks first among cities, while Saudi Arabien (45.0°C) leads countries. These regions maintain consistently hot climates year-round. However, peak single measurements tell a different story. Suva reaches an extraordinary 79.3°C, far exceeding any regional average, mirrored by Fiji Islands' record 79.3°C at the country level. Among cities, Kuwait City peaks at 49.2°C; among countries, Kuwait reaches 49.2°C. Baghdad ranks third at 49.1°C. These top peaks cluster in the Gulf, but none match Suva's anomaly. This suggests extreme heat spikes occur unpredictably across diverse locations, while sustained high temperatures concentrate in arid Middle Eastern zones.
